Run C, round two: the guided tour

One row per line of microgpt_concise.dyalog, in the order of the line-for-line table of design.md, the helper dfns included: the formula, the Dyalog line, the Fortress line or lines of src/MicroGptFlat.fss set by Fortify (verbatim; a ; line of the source is shown one statement per line, and the ASCII source follows in grey), and a note where they differ. The by-eye test of round two is this table.

#formulaDyalogFortress (Fortify)note

L6		⎕IO←0 ⋄ NE BLK NH HD VS BOS←16 16 4 4 27 26 ⋄ EPS LR0 B1 B2 EPSA←1E¯5 0.01 0.85 0.99 1E¯8
(nEmbd, blockSize, nHead, headDim, vocabSize, bosId) = (16, 16, 4, 4, 27, 26)
(epsilon, lr0, beta1, beta2, epsilon_A, nSteps) = (10.0^(-5), 0.01, 0.85, 0.99, 10.0^(-8), 1000)
Index origin is 0 on both sides. The driver's NSTEPS joins the second tuple; the two file paths, which the Dyalog reads "however you like", are a third line not shown.
2
L7		rmsn←{⍵÷(EPS+(+/⍵*2)÷≢⍵)*0.5}
rmsn(x: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = x / SQRT (epsilon + (SUM[t <- x] t^2) / (|x|))
The parameter is a runtime-sized array rather than a nat-generic Vector so that rmsn can be handed to the lift (gap row 156); the sum runs over the elements, not over ⍳≢⍵.
3
L7		sm←{e÷+/e←*⍵-⌈/⍵}
sm(z: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do e = exp(z - (BIG MAX[t <- z] t)); e / (SUM[t <- e] t) end
The Dyalog binds e inside the expression; Fortress binds it in a do block, so the line reads left to right. The max and the sum are the library's reductions.
4
L7		MK←¯1E10×~(⍳BLK)∘.≥⍳BLK
mask: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(blockSize, blockSize, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)
~(⍳BLK)∘.≥⍳BLK is written as its predicate j > i. This is the model's one index lambda; it has no subscript.
5
L8		rmsn_b←{r←(EPS+(+/⍵*2)÷≢⍵)*0.5 ⋄ y←⍵÷r ⋄ (⍺-y×(+/y×⍺)÷≢y)÷r}
rmsn_b(dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], x: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    r = SQRT (epsilon + (SUM[t <- x] t^2) / (|x|))
    y = x / r
    (dy - y ((y DOT dy) / (|y|))) / r
  end
The dfn's three statements, in its order; +/y×⍺ is the dot product y DOT dy. The name keeps the Dyalog's underscore, which Fortify sets literally.
6
L8		sm_b←{⍺×⍵-+/⍺×⍵}
sm_b(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = p × (dy - (p DOT dy))
+/⍺×⍵ is p DOT dy; the outer × is the vocabulary's elementwise product and dy - scalar its scalar extension.
7
L9		SHP←(VS NE)(BLK NE)(VS NE)(NE NE)(NE NE)(NE NE)(NE NE)((4×NE)NE)(NE(4×NE)) ⋄ CNT←×/¨SHP ⋄ OFF←+\0,¯1↓CNT
matName(i: ZZ32): String =
    if i = 0 then "wte" elif i = 1 then "wpe" elif i = 2 then "lm_head" elif i = 3 then "attn_wq" elif i = 4 then "attn_wk"
    elif i = 5 then "attn_wv" elif i = 6 then "attn_wo" elif i = 7 then "mlp_fc1" else "mlp_fc2" end
matShape(i: ZZ32): (ZZ32, ZZ32) =
    if (i = 0) OR (i = 2) then (vocabSize, nEmbd) elif i = 7 then (4 nEmbd, nEmbd) elif i = 8 then (nEmbd, 4 nEmbd) else (nEmbd, nEmbd) end
matCount(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do (r, c) = matShape(i); r c end
matOffset(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = SUM[j <- 0#i] matCount(j)
nParams(): ZZ32 = matOffset(9)
The shapes are a function of the index, not an array of pairs: a typed array literal at top level binds a tuple (ledger row 142). The file names are the price of the Dyalog's ⎕NREAD ⍵ being by index.
8
L10		P←⊃,/,¨{(⍵⊃SHP)⍴⎕NREAD ⍵}¨⍳9 ⋄ M←V←P×0
loadParams(dir: String): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    w(i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do (r, c) = matShape(i); readMatrix(dir "/" matName(i) ".txt", r, c) end
    flat(w(0), w(1), w(2), w(3), w(4), w(5), w(6), w(7), w(8))
  end
⊃,/,¨ is flat, a varargs ravel-and-catenate; the nine reads are spelled out because a comprehension over them is ledger row 96. M←V←P×0 is the driver's two zeros(nParams()).
9
L11		v←{(⍵⊃SHP)⍴P[(⍵⊃OFF)+⍳⍵⊃CNT]}
view(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do (r, c) = matShape(i); viewAt(p, matOffset(i), r, c) end
The Dyalog's v copies the slice; viewAt is a zero-copy, writable Matrix over it, so the same table that reads the weights would write them (Hsu's tactic 8).

L12		TOKM←↑{(BLK+1)↑BOS,(⎕A⍳⍵),BOS}¨docs ⋄ LEN←1+≢¨docs
(corpusTokens, corpusLengths) = loadCorpus(corpusPath, blockSize + 1, bosId)
↑ pads with 0 in the Dyalog; the layout pads with BOS, which loadCorpus does. The causal mask and the validity mask make the difference invisible.
11
L13		STEP←{b←⍵ ⋄ B←≢b ⋄ N←B×BLK ⋄ R←TOKM[b;] ⋄ ids←,R[;⍳BLK] ⋄ tg←,R[;1+⍳BLK] ⋄ vm←,LEN[b]∘.>⍳BLK ⋄ nv←+/vm ⋄ pos←N⍴⍳BLK
step(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
    bsz = |b|
    n = bsz blockSize
    toks = gather(corpusTokens, b)
    ids = ravel(block(toks, 0, 0, bsz, blockSize))
tg = ravel(block(toks, 0, 1, bsz, blockSize))
    vm = ravel(valid(gather(corpusLengths, b), blockSize))
nv = SUM vm
pos = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => r MOD blockSize)
TOKM[b;] is gather; ,R[;⍳BLK] is ravel(block(…)), two views; LEN[b]∘.>⍳BLK is valid. N⍴⍳BLK is written as its formula, r mod BLK, rather than as a cyclic reshape.

L14		wte wpe lm wq wk wv wo f1 f2←v¨⍳9
(wte, wpe, lm, wq, wk, wv, wo, f1, f2) = (view(p, 0), view(p, 1), view(p, 2), view(p, 3), view(p, 4), view(p, 5), view(p, 6), view(p, 7), view(p, 8))
One tuple binding for the strand assignment; every name is a view.

L15		X←wte[ids;]+wpe[pos;] ⋄ Xp←rmsn⍤1⊢X ⋄ X1←rmsn⍤1⊢Xp
x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos)
xp = rows(rmsn, x)
x1 = rows(rmsn, xp)
rmsn⍤1 is rows(rmsn, ·): the lift is a function of the vocabulary, since ⍤ is not an operator character in Fortress and a nat-generic function cannot be an argument (row 156).

L16		Q K Vv←X1∘(+.×⍉)¨wq wk wv ⋄ h←{0 2 1 3⍉(B,BLK,NH,HD)⍴⍵} ⋄ Qh Kh Vh←h¨Q K Vv
h(m: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = heads(m, blockSize, nHead, headDim)
u(t: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = unheads(t, nHead)
(q, k, v) = (x1 wq^T, x1 wk^T, x1 wv^T)
(qh, kh, vh) = (h(q), h(k), h(v))
h is a rank-3 view of the (doc·pos × heads·dim) matrix, not a copy, and u its inverse; u is declared here beside h where the Dyalog declares it at L24. The two definitions sit before the forward pass in the source.

L17		A←sm⍤1⊢MK+⍤2⊢(Qh+.×⍤2⊢⍉⍤2⊢Kh)÷HD*0.5 ⋄ Hc←(N,NE)⍴0 2 1 3⍉A+.×⍤2⊢Vh
a = rows(sm, mask + (qh kh^T) / SQRT (1.0 headDim))
hc = u(a vh)
One line, as in the Dyalog: +.×⍤2 is the batched product, ⍉⍤2 the plane-transpose view, MK+⍤2 the plane-wise sum, sm⍤1 the row lift over planes; nothing is copied but the products' results.
16
L18		X2←Xp+Hc+.×⍉wo ⋄ X3←rmsn⍤1⊢X2 ⋄ M0←X3+.×⍉f1 ⋄ Mr←0⌈M0 ⋄ X4←X2+Mr+.×⍉f2
x2 = xp + hc wo^T
x3 = rows(rmsn, x2)
m0 = x3 f1^T
mr = 0.0 MAX m0
x4 = x2 + mr f2^T
0⌈M0 is 0.0 MAX m0, the scalar extension of the library's MAX.

L19		Pr←sm⍤1⊢X4+.×⍉lm ⋄ loss←-(+/vm×⍟tg⌷⍤0 1⊢Pr)÷nv
pr = rows(sm, x4 lm^T)
loss = -(vm DOT log(pick(pr, tg))) / nv
tg⌷⍤0 1⊢Pr is pick; +/vm×⍟… is written as the dot product of vm with the elementwise log.

L20		dL←(vm÷nv)×⍤0 1⊢Pr-tg∘.=⍳VS ⋄ gLM←(⍉dL)+.×X4 ⋄ dX4←dL+.×lm
dL = diag(vm / nv) (pr - onehot(tg, vocabSize))
gLM = dL^T x4
dX4 = dL lm
(vm÷nv)×⍤0 1 is diag(vm / nv), whose product scales the rows without forming the diagonal (a row-scaling × is gap row 159); tg∘.=⍳VS is onehot.

L21		gF2←(⍉dX4)+.×Mr ⋄ dM0←(dX4+.×f2)×M0>0 ⋄ gF1←(⍉dM0)+.×X3 ⋄ dX3←dM0+.×f1
gF2 = dX4^T mr
dM0 = (dX4 f2) × (m0 > 0.0)
gF1 = dM0^T x3
dX3 = dM0 f1
M0>0 is the 0/1 matrix m0 > 0.0 and × its elementwise product.

L22		dX2←dX4+dX3(rmsn_b⍤1)X2 ⋄ gWO←(⍉dX2)+.×Hc ⋄ dH←h dX2+.×wo
dX2 = dX4 + rows(rmsn_b, dX3, x2)
gWO = dX2^T hc
dh = h(dX2 wo)
dX3(rmsn_b⍤1)X2 is the dyadic lift rows(rmsn_b, dX3, x2), the rows of the two matrices paired.

L23		dVh←(⍉⍤2⊢A)+.×⍤2⊢dH ⋄ dS←(A(sm_b⍤1)dH+.×⍤2⊢⍉⍤2⊢Vh)÷HD*0.5
dVh = a^T dh
dS = rows(sm_b, a, dh vh^T) / SQRT (1.0 headDim)

L24		dQh←dS+.×⍤2⊢Kh ⋄ dKh←(⍉⍤2⊢dS)+.×⍤2⊢Qh ⋄ u←{(N,NE)⍴0 2 1 3⍉⍵} ⋄ dQ dK dV←u¨dQh dKh dVh
dQh = dS kh
dKh = dS^T qh
(dQ, dK, dV) = (u(dQh), u(dKh), u(dVh))

(gWQ, gWK, gWV) = (dQ^T x1, dK^T x1, dV^T x1)

L27		gWTE←(⍉ids∘.=⍳VS)+.×dX ⋄ gWPE←(⍉pos∘.=⍳BLK)+.×dX
gWTE = transpose(onehot(ids, vocabSize)) dX
gWPE = transpose(onehot(pos, blockSize)) dX
transpose(…) and not ^T: a call result may not be followed by a superscript, parenthesised or not (rows 144, 158).
26
L28		loss(⊃,/,¨gWTE gWPE gLM gWQ gWK gWV gWO gF1 gF2)}
  (loss, flat(gWTE, gWPE, gLM, gWQ, gWK, gWV, gWO, gF1, gF2))
end
flat ravels and catenates the nine gradients in layout order, as ⊃,/,¨ does; the result is a gradient in the layout of p.
27
L29		ADAM←{(t lr g)←⍵ ⋄ M∘←(B1×M)+(1-B1)×g ⋄ V∘←(B2×V)+(1-B2)×g*2 ⋄ P∘←P-lr×(M÷1-B1*t)÷EPSA+(V÷1-B2*t)*0.5}
m' = beta1 m + (1 - beta1) g
v' = beta2 v + (1 - beta2) (g × g)
p' = p - (lr (m' / (1 - beta1^t))) / (SQRT (v' / (1 - beta2^t)) + epsilon_A)
(p', m', v')
Pure: the three results are returned rather than assigned to globals. g*2 is g × g. The association is numpy's, (α m̂)/(√v̂ + ε), because the goldens are numpy's; the Dyalog's is α (m̂/(ε + √v̂)).
28
L30		losses←{l g←STEP(≢docs)|(⍵×BSZ)+⍳BSZ ⋄ ADAM(1+⍵)(LR0×1-⍵÷NSTEPS)g ⋄ l}¨⍳RUN
learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / nSteps)
        (l, g) = step(p, keys(bsz, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => (s bsz + i) MOD nDocs()))
        (p, m, v) := adam(p, m, v, g, s + 1, learningRate(s))
The driver keeps (p, m, v) as the loop's three variables where the Dyalog's ADAM updates globals; the loop, the prints and the timing around these lines are not shown.

Lines with no Dyalog counterpart

  • the two ^T declarations (a matrix, and every plane of a rank-3 array): the Dyalog's ⍉ is primitive; Fortress's ^T is declared, in the model because an API cannot declare a postfix operator (ledger row 133, gap row 166).
  • corpus() and nDocs(), accessors for the check and the driver.
  • the run() driver's prints and timing.
